title: Evacuation Simulation and Safe Failover Playbook
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview

This playbook describes how to simulate tenant evacuation scenarios and perform safe failover of private deployments (VPC and on‑prem) with minimal customer impact. It covers the orchestration steps, runbook procedures, automation checks, and rollback criteria for evacuating workloads (e.g., draining a host, evacuating a rack/availability zone, or failing over a regional control plane). The emphasis is on preserving request SLOs, KV cache continuity, and tenancy isolation.

Scope

- Applies to Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on‑prem) managed by the operator control plane.
- Focus on tenant evacuation and orchestrated failover; does not replace regular upgrade/rollback playbooks but complements them.
- Intended for SREs and field operators running controlled drills and customer-directed failovers.

Goals and success criteria

- Functional: No more than 2% increase in 99th-percentile request latency during the controlled failover window for affected tenants.
- Availability: < 1 minute of 5xx spike sustained longer than 30s for any single tenant during simulation.
- Data continuity: KV cache warmness preserved above 60% after handoff (see KV thresholds table).
- Observability: All simulation events are traced with tag operation:evacuation and have audit entries in telemetry with owner and run_id.

Key concepts

- Drain vs Evacuate: "Drain" is graceful termination of new traffic to a node; "Evacuate" includes KV/state handoff, routing updates, and tenant affinity migration.
- KV cache handoff: For large models we transfer hot prefixes via the rwd-kvproxy-state-transfer mechanism (best effort) and rely on prefix cache pre-warming for warmness preservation.
- Backpressure and rate‑limit awareness: Evacuation should not trigger global rate-limit escalations; throttle redirections and burst windows are explicitly allowed.

Owner and contacts

- Primary owner: eng-sre (oncall: eng-sre-primary@redwood.ai)
- Secondary owner: eng-private-deployments (oncall: private-deploys@redwood.ai)
- Escalation: Platform+ (eng-platform-leads)

Pre-simulation checklist (automated where possible)

1. Confirm run_id and create an audit ticket: rwd-ops create-run --type evacuation --target <target-id> --run_id RWD-EVAC-YYYYMMDD-NNN
2. Validate control plane health: rwdctl cp status --region <region> (expect OK)
3. Verify telemetry ingestion: last 10m metrics ok and sampling rate >= 80% for target tenants
4. Ensure available capacity (buffer): free_gpu_slots >= planned_evacuate_slots * 1.2
5. Customer notification (if applicable): inform customer support and confirm maintenance window or pre-agreed SLA exception

Thresholds and alerting table

| Metric | Alert name | Threshold | Action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tenant 99p latency | TenantEvacuationLatencyHigh | 99p increase > 2x baseline for > 2 min | Pause simulation, investigate routing and KV warmness |
| 5xx rate | TenantEvacuation5xxSpike | > 1% request rate for > 30s | Auto-rollback to last stable route. Escalate to oncall |
| KV cache warmness | KVCacheWarmthDrop | warmness < 60% | Trigger pre-warm and extend canary window |
| Ingress drop rate | EvacIngressDrops | drop_rate > 0.5% for > 1 min | Throttle outbound reassignment, verify rate limits |
| Control plane sync lag | CPControlplaneSyncLag | > 10s | Abort; investigate state store connectivity |

Simulation types

- Node drain simulation (low blast radius): simulate taking one GPU host out of service for 10 min.
- Rack/zone evacuation (medium): migrate tenants off an AZ over 15–30 min with staged traffic steering.
- Region failover (high): orchestrated routing change and control plane takeover; used rarely and requires manager approval.
- Partial KV transfer (targeted): test rwd-kvproxy prefix export/import between two nodes to measure re-warm timings.

Run stages (phase-driven automation)

1. Prepare
   - Tag the run with run_id and set operation:evacuation in tracing.
   - Snapshot baseline metrics for affected tenants: latency, error rate, token throughput, cache warmness.
   - Reserve destination capacity: rwdctl capacity reserve --tenants <list> --slots <n> --duration 60m
   - Mark routes as canary-ready: rwd-router mark-canary --routes <routes> --run-id <run_id>
2. Canary traffic shift (10–20% traffic)
   - Shift a small percentage of new sessions to destination pool.
   - Monitor SLOs and KV warmness for 3 consecutive 60s windows.
   - If SLOs hold, proceed to broaden; otherwise trigger rollback.
3. Broad traffic reallocation (60–90%):
   - Use staged weights every 2–5 minutes.
   - For each stage ensure: TenantEvacuationLatencyHigh is not firing and KVCacheWarmthDrop is within tolerated bounds.
4. Final cutover (remaining traffic):
   - Execute last‑session-drain command: rwdctl node drain --id <node> --grace-period 120s
   - Confirm no active streams remain using rwdctl streams list --node <node>
   - Deallocate host from serving pool and mark as maintenance.
5. Post-evac verification
   - Compare baseline and post-evac metrics.
   - Archive traces for the run and attach to audit ticket.
   - Open post-mortem if thresholds breached.

CLI examples

- Reserve capacity:
  rwdctl capacity reserve --tenants tenant-42,tenant-77 --slots 8 --duration 120m --run-id RWD-EVAC-20260815-001

- Start a canary shift:
  rwdctl router shift --route service/tenants/tenant-42 --to dest-pool-west-1 --weight 0.1 --run-id RWD-EVAC-20260815-001

- Check KV cache warmness (per-tenant):
  curl -s http://rwd-kvproxy.metrics/tenants/tenant-42 | jq '.warmness'

KV cache transfer snippet (YAML example)

apiVersion: v1
kind: KVTransfer
metadata:
  run_id: RWD-EVAC-20260815-001
  tenant: tenant-42
spec:
  source_node: node-123
  dest_node: node-456
  prefixes: ["/prompts/", "/prefixes/chat/"]
  mode: best-effort

Note: prefix list should be limited to top 5% hottest prefixes for performance reasons.

Rollback criteria and automated rollback behavior

- Immediate rollback (automatic): if TenantEvacuation5xxSpike fires or 99p latency > 2x baseline for > 2 minutes.
- Conditional rollback (operator decision): KVCacheWarmthDrop persists below 45% after 15 minutes of warm‑up or ingress drops continue past 5 minutes.
- Rollback action: rwdctl router shift --route <route> --to source-pool --weight 1.0 --run-id <run_id> --force

Manual intervention steps

1. Pause orchestration: rwd-ops pause-run --run_id <run_id>
2. Inspect node logs: rwdctl node logs --id <node> --since 30m | grep eviction
3. Temporarily increase token throttles for destination pool to reduce queuing by 20%: rwdctl pool set --pool dest-pool --throttle-token-rate <value>
4. If KV handoff failed: re-run KVTransfer in incremental mode with smaller prefix selections.

Safety controls and limits

- Max concurrent tenant evacuations per region: 5 (hard limit enforced by orchestration layer).
- Max sustained traffic weight change per step: 30% (recommended 10–20% for latency-sensitive tenants).
- Circuit breaker: if any tenant experiences > 0.5% of requests returning 503 repeatedly, automation pauses and alerts oncall.

Observability and traces

- All evacuation runs must have traces with tag: operation:evacuation and run_id: RWD-EVAC-YYYYMMDD-NNN.
- Dashboard: "Evacuation Operations" which shows per-run metrics: traffic weight, cache warmness, 99p latency, 5xx rate, route count.
- Important spans: rwd-router.route-change, rwd-kvproxy.transfer, rwd-controlplane.sync-check.

Simulation validation checklist (post-sim)

- Metric diff summary included in audit ticket and flagged green/yellow/red.
- KV warmness recovered to >= 65% within 20 minutes (green).
- No tenant saw > 1.5x baseline 99p latency for more than 2 minutes (green).
- If any red item, open postmortem and schedule follow-up mitigation.

Dry-run and chaos integration

- Use chaos harness tag "evacuation-dryrun" to run synthetic failures against control plane and routers without touching production tenants.
- Example: chaosctl inject node-failure --node node-123 --duration 120s --tag evacuation-dryrun
- Replay recorded traces to validate alerting rules and automation behavior.

Post-run actions and documentation

1. Attach run artifacts to run ticket: traces, Grafana snapshots, rwdctl logs, KVTransfer logs.
2. Summarize findings and tuning items (e.g., increase pre-warm prefixes, extend canary window).
3. If escalation occurred, schedule a retrospective with engineering, field ops, and support.

Appendix: Quick reference commands

- Start run: rwd-ops create-run --type evacuation --target <target-id> --run_id <id>
- Pause run: rwd-ops pause-run --run_id <id>
- Force rollback: rwdctl router shift --route <route> --to source-pool --weight 1.0 --force --run-id <id>
- Check streams: rwdctl streams list --node <node>

Related pages and learning resources

- Refer to runtime-configuration-drift-detection-and-automated-heal-playbook for automated healing integrations.
